# Agent instructions

## Direction and authority

Read the root objective, README, selected objective, its ancestors, children, and linked dependencies. Preserve founder-authored objective text unless explicitly authorized to revise it. Keep communication concise.

The root is CEO, controlled by the founder. CIO owns graphlang/; CTO owns graphbrowser/; COO/CFO owns meta/. Further depths default to Upper Leadership, Senior Engineer, Junior Engineer, then Apprentice/Intern; deeper nodes retain Apprentice/Intern unless the founder defines another level. Titles describe responsibility, not separate people or automatically spawned agents.

Before writing, identify your assigned objective directory. Edit only files inside that directory and its descendants, including child objectives and local status logs. Read ancestors and siblings for context, but request their owner's changes through your local status log. A title or dependency link grants no additional write authority. Root/CEO assignment and edits to root AGENTS.md or README.md require explicit founder authorization; never infer root assignment from repository access. Existing children owned by other active agents require coordination before overlapping edits.

Graph Lang source/docs live in oasislaboratory/graph-lang. An assignment here does not itself grant write authority in another repository. This repository coordinates objectives and evidence across the three branches.

## Select and act

1. Within your assigned subtree, select the oldest unfinished, unblocked leaf by the Git commit that introduced its objective.md; break ties by path. A leaf has no child objective folders. Missing status means unfinished.
2. Estimate confidence in completing and verifying that leaf in one run. Record a short rationale; this is a judgment, not measured probability.
3. If confidence is at least 50%, execute the bounded work and verify the result.
4. Otherwise create two to four child folders, each with an objective.md and metadata. Each child should have >50% estimated confidence of being achievable through execution or further recursive decomposition. Explain why the set plausibly advances and covers the parent.
5. Intermediate objectives may require later decomposition. Children need not make the parent achievable in one subsequent run. Product-market fit requires longitudinal evidence.
6. Expand only the selected leaf in a run. Stop after decomposition; avoid speculative trees. If blocked, record the missing input and select another eligible leaf within your scope when possible.

## Objective metadata

Each objective.md starts with YAML fields:

- role: responsibility title for its depth.
- status: planned, in_progress, ongoing, blocked, completed, or cancelled.
- progress_percent: 0–100 estimate against explicit acceptance criteria; null when no defensible baseline exists.
- confidence_percent: 0–100 estimated chance of completing and verifying the stated next action in one run; null before assessment.
- assessed_by: actual model identifier if available, otherwise an honest agent label; null before assessment.
- assessed_on: assessment date in YYYY-MM-DD format; null before assessment.
- scope: repository-relative directory containing this objective.

Keep strategic mandates ongoing. Start bounded children planned; mark in_progress when work starts. Use blocked only for a concrete unmet prerequisite. Completed requires linked verification against the objective's acceptance criteria; cancelled means intentionally stopped.

Reassess percentages when working a node, with rationale and evidence in its local status.md. Distinguish estimated progress from next-action confidence. Do not invent precision, increase progress merely for creating children, or average child percentages without explicit weights and criteria. Continuing mandates can remain ongoing as individual milestones complete.

## Evidence and learning

Keep a brief status.md beside the selected objective: action assessed, confidence/progress rationale, result, verification links, and next dependency. objective.md metadata is the canonical current status; status.md supplies its supporting record. Distinguish plans, source inspection, tested behavior, and customer evidence. Parent owners reconcile their own status; child agents report evidence without editing ancestors.

For Meta experiments, define the hypothesis, baseline, variants, evaluation tasks, metric, budget, and stopping rule before running. Compare equivalent tasks under comparable budgets; record failures and cost as well as wins. Avoid selecting policies solely on their own self-reported scores.

Founder retains vision and veto authority. Surface consequential direction changes for a decision. Follow the current task's authorization for repository writes; an objective alone does not authorize external outreach or financial transactions.

Folder scope is an agent operating policy, not technical access enforcement. Do not claim GitHub prevents out-of-scope writes.

## COO/CFO advisory authority

COO/CFO may review the entire OKR DAG and propose edits or alternative (forked) structures for any branch, the root objective, role boundaries, agent instructions, prompts, or workflow. This cross-tree advisory remit supports workflow research and controlled A/B testing; it does not expand direct write scope.

Store proposals, patches, and alternative-tree fixtures under meta/, referencing the source commit and affected paths. Include the hypothesis, proposed changes, baseline/variant comparison, evidence or planned test, expected tradeoffs, and a clear proposed/approved/rejected disposition. Label simulations and untested variants honestly.

Founder approval is required before applying a proposal outside meta/ or changing shared policies, permissions, prompts, or schedules. A proposed fork is an artifact or design under meta/, not authorization to create a GitHub fork or change the live tree. Chief of Staff should surface material proposals in its read-only dashboard.

# Oasis

[Root objective](objective.md): cultivate this OKR DAG into a startup reaching product-market fit for its olog / graph browser / IDE.

| Role / branch | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| CIO / [Graph Lang](graphlang/objective.md) | Language, runtime, source, and documentation in the separate graph-lang repository. |
| CTO / [Graph Browser](graphbrowser/objective.md) | Hosted dashboard / IDE with Graph Lang execution and a persistent database/environment. |
| COO/CFO / [Meta](meta/objective.md) | The OKR DAG, agent portfolios, performance-based allocation, and experiments on the process itself. |

Each objective folder is a node. Nested objective folders are key results that can themselves be decomposed. Use relative Markdown links for cross-branch dependencies and shared results; do not duplicate work or introduce dependency cycles.

Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before selecting or expanding work. These three branches are strategic objectives, not completed results or a claim that product-market fit is guaranteed.

## Roles and status

The root is CEO, controlled by the founder. CIO owns Graph Lang; CTO owns Graph Browser; COO/CFO owns Meta. Deeper objective folders represent Upper Leadership → Senior Engineer → Junior Engineer → Apprentice/Intern. These are responsibility levels; create them only when useful objectives require decomposition.

Every objective carries YAML metadata: `role`, `status`, `progress_percent`, `confidence_percent`, `assessed_by`, `assessed_on`, and `scope`. Current strategic objectives are `ongoing`; percentages are `null` until assessed against evidence and a bounded next action.

Status: `planned` → `in_progress` → `completed`; use `ongoing` for continuing mandates, `blocked` for a missing prerequisite, and `cancelled` for intentionally stopped work.

Agents may edit only their explicitly assigned objective folder and descendants. Ancestors and linked dependencies are readable; sibling changes go to their owner. Root/CEO assignment and shared policy changes require explicit founder authorization. This is an agent operating policy, not a GitHub permission boundary; technical isolation requires scoped tooling or separate review controls.

# Upper Leadership — Define a falsifiable OKR browser workflow

Specify the smallest useful Graph Browser increment using Oasis's OKR DAG as a concrete workflow. Produce a pinned, read-only input fixture and acceptance scenarios within this folder.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identify the initial user, task, and hypothesized benefit as assumptions to test, not established demand.
- Define graph/objective identity, parent/child and cross-dependency links, objective/status metadata, and preservation of source text for the fixture.
- Describe an end-to-end task: open the DAG, inspect a leaf and its evidence/dependencies, propose an edit, save it to a test environment, reload, and compare the result with the intended change.
- Specify deterministic pass/fail checks, malformed/missing-data behavior, and what an observed usability result would support or refute.
- Separate fixture/simulation acceptance from real runtime, durable storage, hosting, and customer validation. List required interfaces and unresolved decisions without committing to a provider.

Next action: author and validate the fixture/scenarios against the pinned source. Confidence 90%; bounded specification and fixture checks fit one run.

# Upper Leadership — Verify runtime and persistent environment boundaries

Define and verify the Graph Browser's integration with Graph Lang execution and a persistent database/environment. Coordinate against the [Graph Lang objective](../../graphlang/objective.md) using read-only inspection and local requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Specify versioned graph input/output, environment lookup, execution result/error, and persistence adapter boundaries with executable fixture checks where feasible.
- Distinguish graph representation, browser navigation, evaluation, and persistent state. Do not treat loading JSON as executing Graph Lang.
- Verify real adapters when available; preserve requests and acceptance cases for missing runtime capabilities without claiming mock results as integration success.
- Demonstrate save/reload durability at the declared storage boundary plus invalid input, failed-write, and conflicting-version behavior. State which restart/session failures the chosen boundary covers.
- Keep runtime/storage proposals reversible and within this folder. Request founder decisions before consequential architecture or external access changes.

Dependency: [workflow contract](../01-workflow-contract/objective.md). A real-runtime verification milestone additionally depends on an available documented Graph Lang runtime.
Next action once eligible: inspect required interfaces and create a bounded adapter/conformance plan or decompose its implementation. Confidence 75% for that next action; actual runtime readiness is unknown.

- Separate local verification from deployed behavior and customer observations. Record absent evidence honestly; a successful build is not product-market fit.
- Deliver deployment-ready artifacts or a concrete deployment plan in this folder and identify founder approvals required for hosting and participant access.
- Mark completed only when this preparation package is verified; actual deployment and outreach require separate authorization and follow-up objectives.

Dependency: the preceding prototype and integration packages; do not report hosted readiness while their acceptance requirements remain unmet.
Next action once eligible: inspect the available evidence and author a bounded release/validation plan or decompose remaining preparation. Confidence 80% for that next action; no confidence estimate of customer adoption is claimed.

# Upper Leadership — Predefine a controlled process experiment

Using [the baseline](../01-baseline/objective.md), preregister one bounded A/B comparison of the agent work process. Define the protocol before running either variant.

Acceptance criteria:
- State a falsifiable hypothesis, baseline/control A, and exactly one changed process rule in variant B.
- Specify comparable task fixtures, fixed acceptance checks, actual model configuration when known, assignment/randomization method, per-variant work budget, and handling of failed or missing runs.
- Define primary verified-outcome metric, rework/quality checks, elapsed time and cost where measurable, sample size, stopping rule, and the threshold for an allocation recommendation. Never use self-reported confidence as the success metric.
- Provide a frozen task/evaluation manifest and explain how to keep evaluation separate from variant self-scoring. Label the comparison exploratory if sample size cannot support a stronger conclusion.
- Keep execution within Meta's folder and existing authority; propose, rather than change, other chiefs' prompts, schedules, or allocations.

Dependency: baseline schema and available measurement limitations must be documented first.
Next action once eligible: write and validate the protocol/manifest. Conditional confidence: 85%; a bounded protocol can be authored and checked, while measurement gaps may limit what can be tested.

# Upper Leadership — Evaluate variants and recommend allocation

Run the [preregistered comparison](../02-experiment-design/objective.md) within its defined scope and budget, then report whether evidence supports changing allocation. Do not modify schedules, other branches, financial assets, or spending.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preserve the frozen protocol reference and raw records for both variants, including failures, missing measurements, verification outputs, model identity when available, and deviations.
- Evaluate both variants against the same independent acceptance checks; report paired or otherwise protocol-defined comparisons and limitations.
- Apply the stopping rule and recommendation threshold without changing them after seeing results. State inconclusive when evidence is insufficient.
- Propose retain/change/collect-more-evidence with rationale, expected tradeoffs, and a bounded next iteration for evolutionary improvement. Any consequential allocation change remains a founder decision.

Dependency: baseline and frozen experiment protocol; execution is ineligible until those exist. If the protocol is too large for one run, decompose this objective before executing it.
Next action once eligible: inspect the frozen protocol and execute a bounded comparison or decompose its execution. Conditional confidence: 70% through bounded execution or further decomposition; confidence in demonstrating an improvement is unknown.

# COO/CFO — Meta

Evolve this OKR DAG into an effective system for directing Oasis and optimizing portfolios of agents and their work.

Have agents manage portfolios of objectives and experiments; measure outcomes, learn from performance, and allocate effort accordingly. Test improvements to the process itself through controlled A/B experiments and evolutionary variation, selection, and iteration.

Evaluate allocation policies against a baseline using verified objective progress, quality, cost, and elapsed time. Treat gains as hypotheses until measured; distinguish agent/work portfolios from financial portfolios, which require an explicit mandate.

## Advisory remit

Review the full OKR DAG and suggest edits or forked structures to improve workflow. Keep evidence, proposals, patches, and test variants within meta/; applying changes elsewhere requires founder approval. See [COO/CFO advisory authority](../AGENTS.md#coocfo-advisory-authority).
